SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.claim: The fire passage describes its condition without threatening to remove it: people can live without fire, but not without food or water.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p709/r2.anchor: لأن الناس يمكن أن يعيشوا بلا نار لكن لا يمكنهم أن يعيشوا بلا طعام أو ماء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r1.claim: The fire and zaqqūm of Hell are real: as God combines fire and tree in the worldly markh and ʿafār, He can create zaqqūm in Hell; this answers Quraysh's mockery of 17:60.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p157/r1.anchor: people who regard the union of fire and tree in Hell as impossible should learn a lesson from this tree in which God has combined both

QASHANI:56:73-82/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:56:73-82/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:56:73-82/r1.claim: The fire is a reminder of the primordial covenant and a provision for those lacking knowledge and practice as supplies for spiritual wayfaring.
QASHANI:56:73-82/r1.anchor: تذكيرا للعهد الأزلي في العالم القدسي { ومتاعا } للذين لا زاد لهم في السلوك

QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r1.claim: The fire is a reminder of the promised Fire of the afterlife and a provision for travelers who benefit from it on journeys.
QUSHAYRI:v3p279/r1.anchor: يتذكر بها الإنسان ما توعده به في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p90/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p90/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p90/r1.claim: The fire serves as a reminder of Hell and a provision for people camped in barren land or travelers; Ibn Zayd's gloss 'the hungry' is very weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p90/r1.anchor: ومتاعا للمقوين: أي النازلين الأرض القوا، وهي القفر

NAHHAS:v4p341/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p341/r7.claim: The phrase is parsed as two objects, meaning the fire is a reminder.

NAHHAS:v4p341/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p341/r8.anchor: روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال المقوون المسافرون

NAHHAS:v4p341/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p341/r10.claim: The root means that a house became empty; a cited poem uses aqwā and aqfara for an abandoned dwelling.
NAHHAS:v4p341/r10.anchor: أصل هذا من أقوت الدار أي خلت كما قال

NAHHAS:v4p341/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p341/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p341/r11.claim: Aqwā also means settling in barren land, or that one's companions are free of weakness.
NAHHAS:v4p341/r11.anchor: ويقال أقوى إذا نزل بالقي أي الأرض الخالية وأقوى إذا قوي أصحابه أي خلوا من الضعف

ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r3.claim: The fire reminds its viewer of Hell and its punishment, prompting remembrance of God and seeking refuge from Hell.
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r3.anchor: أي إذا رآها الرائي ذكر جهنم وما يخافه من العذاب، فذكر الله عز وجل واستجار به منها

ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r4.claim: Al-muqwī is a traveler who comes to al-qawāʾ, a desolate, empty land.
ZAJJAJ:v5p115/r4.anchor: ومعنى (متاعا للمقوين)، المقوي الذي ينزل بالقواء.

THALABI:v9p217/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p217/r2.claim: The fire is a provision and benefit for people who camp in the open, because the wilderness is empty of habitation.
THALABI:v9p217/r2.anchor: ومتاعا بلغة ومنفعة للمقوين المسافرين النازلين في الأرض القي والقوى

THALABI:v9p217/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p217/r3.claim: Most commentators take the beneficiaries as travelers and residents alike, who use fire for light, warmth, cooking, and remembering Hell to seek refuge from it.
THALABI:v9p217/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد للمقوين يعني للمستمتعين من الناس أجمعين، المسافرين والحاضرين يستضيء بها

THALABI:v9p217/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v9p217/r4.claim: Hasan says the fire is a provision carried by travelers in cloths and saddle-bags.
THALABI:v9p217/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: بلغة المسافرين يبلغون بها إلى أسفارهم يحملونها في الخرق والجواليق

THALABI:v9p217/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r5.speaker: الربيع والسدي
THALABI:v9p217/r5.claim: Al-Rabi and al-Suddi explain the verse as serving destitute people without provisions, who kindle fire to bake food; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas.
THALABI:v9p217/r5.anchor: وقال الربيع والسدي: يعني للمرملين المعترين الذين لا زاد معهم، نارا يوقدون فيختبزون

THALABI:v9p217/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v9p217/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fire serves the hungry; Arabs also used aqwā to mean that a person had eaten nothing.
THALABI:v9p217/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: للجائعين. تقول العرب: أقويت مذ كذا وكذا أي ما أكلت شيئا

THALABI:v9p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p217/r7.speaker: قطرب
THALABI:v9p217/r7.claim: Qutrub says muqwin is a word of opposites, meaning either poverty or wealth, as when someone's animals grow strong or his possessions increase.
THALABI:v9p217/r7.anchor: قال قطرب: المقوي من الأضداد يكون بمعنى الفقر ويكون بمعنى الغنى.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r2.claim: The fire reminds people of Hell and benefits travelers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:56:71-75/r2.anchor: { نحن جعلناها تذكرة } يتذكر بها نار جهنم { ومتاعا } ومنفعة

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r22.claim: Fire is a reminder because livelihood depends on it and it exemplifies life's struggle; it also recalls the punishment of Hellfire.
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r22.anchor: maîşet sebepleri kendisine rabt olunup hayat mücadelesine numûne

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r23.claim: Matāʿ means an enjoyment, useful benefit, and a means of livelihood or gain.
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r23.anchor: hem de bir metâ‘, bir temettu‘, bir intifâ‘ve kazanç vâsıtası

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r24.claim: Al-muqwīn are desert travelers who camp and move on; they benefit especially from fire because they need to kindle it more than settled people do.
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r24.anchor: ondan en ziyade onlar istifade ederler.

ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:56:58-74#2/r25.claim: Another interpretation takes al-muqwīn as poor people with great need, who gather and sell wood when they have no other livelihood.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r7.claim: Given that tree, the author translates muqwin literally as desert travelers and hungry people, for whom fire helps cook food or earn a livelihood by selling it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r7.anchor: Buna göre 73. âyetteki mukvîn kelimesinin de sözlük anlamıyla “çöl yolcuları ve açlık çekenler” diye çevrilmesi uygun olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r8.claim: Beyond its literal sense, fire illustrates the importance of combustion and light in human life and the role of controlled fire in civilization.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r8.anchor: burada ateşin, sürtünme yoluyla meydana gelen yanma olayının, hatta daha geniş bir yorumla ışığın insan hayatındaki önemine, yine ateşin kontrol edilebilir hale gelmesinin medeniyetin oluşmasındaki rolüne dikkat çeken bir örneklendirme yapıldığı söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r9.claim: The author translates tadhkira as “sign” based on context and flow, in line with Mujahid's interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r9.anchor: Buradaki tezkire kelimesine, bağlam ve sözün akışı dikkate alınarak meâlde “işaret” anlamı verilmiştir, Mücâhid’in yorumu da bu yöndedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r10.claim: Many exegetes understand tadhkira as admonition and say fire here reminds people of the punishment of Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r10.anchor: Birçok müfessir ise belirtilen kelimeyi “ibret” mânasında anlamış ve bu ifadede, ateşin cehennem azabını hatırlatıcı yönüne işaret bulunduğunu belirtmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r11.claim: In context, the expression chiefly urges reflection on God's blessings and the conclusion that He can resurrect people after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r11.anchor: Bağlam göz önüne alındığında bu ifadenin öncelikle Allah’ın insanlara verdiği nimetler üzerinde düşünüp sonuçlar çıkarma ve özellikle O’nun insanları öldükten sonra diriltmeye kadir olduğu yargısına ulaşma

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r12.claim: Esed interprets the passage as reminding people that God is the light of the heavens and the earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:56:57/r12.anchor: Muhammed Esed ise burada insana “Allah’ın göklerin ve yerin nûru olduğu”nun hatırlatıldığı yorumunu yapar

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r1.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the fire is a benefit for travelers, named for camping in barren country.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك: أي منفعة للمسافرين سموا بذلك لنزولهم القوى وهو القفر

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the designation muqwin applies to travelers who camp in empty land; related forms qawāʾ and qawāʾ are also used of an uninhabited stopping place and a deserted home.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r2.anchor: الفراء: إنما يقال للمسافرين: مقوين إذا نزلوا القي وهي الأرض القفر التي لا شيء فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r3.speaker: النابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse uses aqwat of a house emptied of inhabitants over time.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r3.anchor:
قال النابغة:
يا دار مية بالعلياء فالسند
أقوت وطال عليها سالف الأمد

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r4.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r4.claim: ʿAntara’s verse uses aqwā and aqfar for an ancient, deserted encampment.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r4.anchor:
وقال عنترة:
حييت من طلل تقادم عهده
أقوى وأقفر بعد أم الهيثم

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r5.claim: Related forms also describe becoming powerful or a traveler camping in the wilderness.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r5.anchor: ويقال: أقوى أي قوي وقوي أصحابه، وأقوى إذا سافر أي نزل القواء والقي

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r6.claim: Mujāhid takes the fire as useful to everyone for cooking, baking, warmth, and light, and as a reminder of Hellfire from which people seek refuge.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: { للمقوين } المستمتعين بها من الناس أجمعين في الطبخ والخبز والاصطلاء والاستضاءة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says it benefits the hungry in preparing food; aqwaytu means going without food, and spending the night in qiwāʾ or qafr means hungry without a meal.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: للجائعين في إصلاح طعامهم. يقال: أقويت منذ كذا وكذا، أي ما أكلت شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r8.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r8.claim: An unnamed poet uses al-quwā for hunger, saying he chooses it while empty-stomached rather than be called mean.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r8.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وإني لأختار القوى طاوي الحشى
محافظة من أن يقال لئيم

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r9.speaker: الربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r9.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and al-Suddī, also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās by al-ʿAwfī, explain muqwin as people without fire-starting sticks to light a fire and bake.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r9.anchor: وقال الربيع والسدي: { المقوين } المنزلين الذين لا زناد معهم يعني نارا يوقدون

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r10.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r10.claim: Quṭrub calls muqwin a word with opposite senses: poor without provisions and wealthy with strong mounts and abundant property.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r10.anchor: وقال قطرب: المقوي من الأضداد يكون بمعنى الفقير ويكون بمعنى الغني

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r11.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r11.claim: Al-Mahdawī says the verse encompasses all, since travelers and residents, rich and poor, need fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r11.anchor: المهدوي: والآية تصلح للجميع لأن النار يحتاج إليها المسافر والمقيم والغني والفقير

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r12.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r12.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says most exegetes follow the first interpretation, travelers.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r12.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي أن أكثر المفسرين على القول الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r13.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī says travelers are singled out because they need fire more: desert people light it at night to repel predators and for many other needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:73-74/r13.anchor: القشيري: وخص المسافر بالانتفاع بها لأن انتفاعه بها أكثر من منفعة المقيم

TABATABAI:56:63-74/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r9.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says al-maqwin is a traveler or resident in an empty tract, and aqwat al-dar means the house became empty of its people.
TABATABAI:56:63-74/r9.anchor: والمقوي النازل بالقواء من الأرض ليس بها أحد، وأقوت الدار خلت من أهلها.

SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r1.claim: أقوى الرجل means that someone settled in a barren, empty tract, like أصحر means entering open desert.
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r1.anchor: أقوى الرجل: إذا حل في الأرض القواء، وهي القفر، كأصحر: دخل في الصحراء

SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r2.claim: أقوت الدار means a house became empty; al-Nabigha's verse uses أقوت of an abandoned home.
SAMIN-DURR:56:73/r2.anchor: وأقوت الدار: خلت، من ذلك لأنها تصير قفرا. قال النابغة

ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n24/r1.claim: Fire, as a source of human light, reminds people that God is the light of the heavens and earth (24:35).
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n24/r1.anchor: is the source of all light known to man, it is apt to remind him

ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r1.claim: Muqwin comes from qawiya, to become deserted or desolate; qawa' or qiwa means desert, wilderness, wasteland, hunger or starvation, so muqwin can mean hungry or lost in a deserted place.

ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r2.claim: Asad rejects limiting the word to desert wayfarers and renders it tropically for lonely, unfortunate, confused people hungering for human warmth and spiritual light.
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r2.anchor: difficult to imagine that, as some commentators assume

ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r3.claim: His composite rendering, 'all who are lost and hungry in the wilderness,' works literally and tropically for those who hunger for human warmth and spiritual light.
ASAD-NOTES:56:73#n25/r3.anchor: My composite rendering of al-muqwin as

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p273/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p273/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p273/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the provision for those in need as provision for a traveler.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p273/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ومتاعا للمقوين ﴾ قال للمسافر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r1.claim: The resumed sentence specifies the fire’s benefits: it reminds people of Hell because God made livelihood depend on fire, inviting them to remember its punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r1.anchor: جعلناها تذكيرا لنار جهنم حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعاش

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r2.claim: An alternative takes earthly fire as a model of Hellfire, which is seventy times hotter according to the report in the two Sahih collections.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r2.anchor: ناركم هذه توقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r3.claim: The Prophet says, in a report found in the two Sahih collections, that the fire people kindle is one part of seventy parts of Hellfire.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ناركم هذه توقدون جزء من سبعين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r4.claim: On either account, تذكرة means remembrance opposite to forgetting; the first account does not address whether earthly fire is of Hell’s kind, while the second does.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r4.anchor: وعلى الوجهين التذكرة من الذكر المقابل للنسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r5.claim: Another view makes the fire a proof of resurrection: bringing fire from green wood shows God can restore dispersed matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r5.anchor: من أخرج من النار من الشجر الأخضر المضاد لها قادر على إعادة ما تفرقت مواده

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r6.claim: The proposed sense illumination in darkness is rejected because تذكرة cannot mean visual perception derived from sight.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r6.anchor: وفيه أن التذكرة لا تكون بمعنى التبصرة المأخوذة من البصر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r7.claim: Many authorities, including Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada, transmit the explanation that the fire reminds people of Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r7.anchor: وكون المراد تذكرة لنار جهنم هو المأثور عن الكثيرين ومنهم ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r8.claim: متاع means benefit or useful provision for those in need of fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r8.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي الفقر من أقوى دخل كأصحر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r9.claim: The المقوون are people who enter barren land; القواء denotes desolation or poverty, as أقوى parallels أصحر, entered the desert.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r9.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي الفقر من أقوى دخل كأصحر دخل الصحراء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r10.claim: Barren-land dwellers are singled out because they need fire most; residents or nearby travelers are not compelled to kindle it with fire-sticks.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r10.anchor: وتخصيص المقوين بذلك لأنهم أحوج إليها فإن المقيمين أو النازلين بقرب منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r11.claim: Another explanation takes المقوين as travelers; reports from Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Qatada describe travelers running out of supplies and using fire to warm themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r11.anchor: عبد بن حميد عن الحسن وهو وابن جرير وعبد الرزاق عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r12.claim: Travelers are called المقوين because they often cross barren lands and deserts.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r12.anchor: وكان إطلاق المقوين على المسافرين لأنهم كثيرا ما يسلكون الفقراء والمفاوز

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r13.claim: A further view identifies the المقوين as poor people, who use fire for light and warmth; أقوى is explained as becoming poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r13.anchor: يستضيئون بها في الظلمة ويصطلحون من البرد كأنه تصور من حال الحاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says المقوون are the hungry, with empty stomachs and provisions, who need fire to cook their food.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r14.anchor: لأنهم أقوت أي خلت بطونهم ومزاودهم من الطعام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r15.claim: The hungry-only explanation is remote because their needs and relief are not limited to foods that require cooking.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r15.anchor: وتعقب بأنه بعيد لعدم انحصار ما يهمهم ويسد خلتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r16.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r16.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say the fire benefits all people, travelers and residents, by providing light, warmth, cooking, and baking.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r16.anchor: الموقين المستمتعين بها من الناس أجمعين المسافرين والحاضرين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r17.speaker: الطيبي والطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r17.claim: Al-Tibi and al-Tabarsi explain المقوي as a word of opposites: poor for lacking wealth and rich for having power over what one wants.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150/r17.anchor: وعلى هذا القول المقوى من الأضداد يقال للفقير

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi questions the opposites account and finds it more plausible that المقوي means one in need, since all who enjoy fire need it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r1.anchor: ولعل الأقرب عليه أنه أريد بالأقواء الأحتياج والمستمتع محتاج إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r2.claim: The fire’s worldly benefit is mentioned last to draw attention to the more important, otherworldly benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r2.anchor: لتنبيه على الأهم هو النفع الأخروي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r3.claim: Water precedes fire because it is more urgently and widely needed and more generally useful.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r3.anchor: الاحتياج إليه أشد وأكثر والانتفاع به أعم وأوفر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r4.claim: An alternative order goes from creating humans to food, water for kneading it, then fire for baking it; al-Alusi calls this rationale unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r4.anchor: ذكر بعده ما به قوام الإنسان من فائدة الحرث وهو الطعام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r5.speaker: حجر المروزي عن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r5.claim: Hujr al-Marwazi heard Ali recite the prior rhetorical questions about procreation, crops, water, and fire, replying ‘Rather, You, Lord’ three times after each.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r5.anchor: حجر المروي قال : بت عند علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r6.claim: Scholars disagree over whether it is recommended to answer each rhetorical question in ritual prayer with ‘Rather, You, Lord.’
ALUSI-FULL:v27p150#2/r6.anchor: استحسان قول مثل ذلك في الصلاة اختلافا بين العلماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r8.claim: They say worldly fire reminds anyone who sees it of the greater fire, Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r8.anchor: تذكرة للنار الكبرى إذا رآها الرائي ذكر جهنم قاله عكرمة ومجاهد ومقاتل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r9.claim: Ata says the fire is an admonition by which the believer takes warning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#2/r9.anchor: وقال عطاء: موعظة يتعظ بها المؤمن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r2.claim: Most exegetes take “muqwin” as travelers or people in desolate country; the root refers to a barren, uninhabited place, and an empty house is said to have “aqwat.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r2.anchor: للمقوين} المسافرين و"المقوي": النازل في الأرض والقي والقوا هو: القفر الخالية البعيدة من العمران،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r3.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r3.claim: Fire benefits desert dwellers and travelers especially: at night they use it to deter beasts, guide the lost, and for other needs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أنه ينتفع بها أهل البوادي والأسفار، فإن منفعتهم بها أكثر من منفعة المقيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r4.claim: They say all people, travelers and residents alike, enjoy the fire for light, warmth, cooking, and baking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة: "للمقوين" يعني للمستمتعين بها من الناس أجمعين، المسافرين والحاضرين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan understands it as a provision for travelers, who carry it in cloths and bags to sustain themselves on journeys.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: بلغة للمسافرين، يتبلغون بها إلى أسفارهم، يحملونها في الخرق والجواليق.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd takes it to mean the hungry; the idiom “aqwaytu” means that one has eaten nothing for a while.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: للجائعين تقول العرب: أقويت منذ كذا وكذا أي: ما أكلت شيئا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r7.speaker: قطرب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r7.claim: Qutrub says “muqwi” is an opposite: it can mean poor for lack of wealth or rich and powerful; the fire benefits both rich and poor, and no one can do without it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p21#3/r7.anchor: قال قطرب: "المقوي" من الأضداد، يقال للفقير: مقو لخلوه من المال، ويقال للغني: مقو، لقوته على ما يريد،

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r9.claim: Fire is a reminder and sign of resurrection, or a reminder in darkness and model of Hellfire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r9.anchor: تبصرة في أمر البعث كما مر في سورة «يس»

BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r10.claim: The fire benefits travelers in barren country, or those whose stomachs or provisions are empty; the latter sense derives from a deserted house.
BAYDAWI-FULL:56:68-73/r10.anchor: للمقوين } الذين ينزلون القواء وهي القفر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r9.claim: The emphatic ‘We’ means God alone made the fire a reminder of resurrection, the punishment of the greater Fire, the tree of Zaqqūm, and other realities revealed to the perceptive.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r9.anchor: بما اقتضته عظمتنا , وقدم من منافعها ما هو أولى بسياق البعث

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r10.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r10.claim: Ibn Barrajān compares striking fire from wood to the cry among people and to God’s creation of bodies from the unseen; the greater Fire lies hidden beyond the visible world.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن برجان : فوزان قدح الزناد من الشجر , والزناد وزان الصيحة بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r11.claim: God made fire a constant reminder of what people light with it, making reflection and admonition more likely.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r11.anchor: وعلق بحا سبحانه كثيرا من أسباب المعاش التي لا غنى عنها ليكون مذكرا لهم بما أوقدوا به حاضرا دائما

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r12.claim: Fire is a lasting, indispensable means for livelihood and reaching one’s aims, providing light, warmth, cooking, processing, melting, hardening, and protection from predators.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r12.anchor: أي إنشاء وبقاء وتعميرا ونفعا وإيصالا إلى غاية المراد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r13.claim: ‘For the hungry’ refers to empty bellies; it also refers to those who arrive in barren, remote wilderness, and anyone suited to such a wasteland can bear the description even when elsewhere.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r13.anchor: أي الجياع الذي أقوت بطونهم - أي خلت -

BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r14.claim: Al-qiwāʾ is a barren wilderness, far from habitation, broad, empty, and remote.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p420#2/r14.anchor: والقواء بالكسر والمد أي القفر الخالية المتباعدة الأطراف البعيدة من العمران

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as a reminder of the greater Fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما نحن جعلناها تذكرة قال : تذكرة للنار الكبرى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-muqwin as travelers.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3334#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما نحن جعلناها تذكرة قال : تذكرة للنار الكبرى ومتاعا للمقوين قال : للمسافرين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r6.claim: Matāʿ means something enjoyed or used for a time; Ibn ʿĀshūr points to the phrase “the enjoyment of this world is little” in al-Nisāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r6.anchor: والمتاع : ما يتمتع ، أي ينتفع به زمانا ، وتقدم في قوله : { قل متاع الدنيا قليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r7.claim: Al-muqwī can mean someone in a barren desert, and also a hungry person whose stomach is empty; both senses derive from emptiness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r7.anchor: والمقوي : الداخل في القواء ( بفتح القاف والمد ) وهي القفر ، ويطلق المقوي على الجائع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r8.claim: Fire benefits travelers by lighting and warming camps, guiding night travelers to shelter, and enabling people to cook while hungry, at home or on journeys.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r8.anchor: فإن النار متاع للمسافرين يستضيئون بها في مناخهم ويصطلون بها في البرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r9.claim: The word gathers both desert traveler and hungry-person senses, folding a reminder of divine favor into the argument; these groups need fire especially.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p326/r9.anchor: فإيثار هذا الوصف في هذه الآية ليجمع المعنيين فإن النار متاع للمسافرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r9.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r9.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain the fire as a reminder of the fire of Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r9.anchor: و: تذكرة معناه: تذكر نار جهنم، قاله مجاهد وقتادة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r10.claim: Matāʿ means something from which people benefit.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r11.claim: Al-muqwīn are people in barren country or deserts; Ibn Atiyya says the other explanations do not match the usage as well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r11.anchor: والمقوي في هذه الآية: الكائن في الأرض القواء وهي الفيافي،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd's gloss of al-muqwīn as hungry people is one of several weak interpretations, in Ibn Atiyya's view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r12.anchor: وعبر الناس في تفسير «المقوين» بأشياء ضعيفة، كقول ابن زيد للجائعين ونحوه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses them as travelers, a wording Ibn Atiyya says comes close to his own sense of people entering barren country.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r13.anchor: ومن قال معناه: للمسافرين، فهو نحو ما قلناه، وهي عبارة ابن عباس رضي الله عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r14.claim: The root usage means entering a barren land, as in saying a man entered morning or entered the open desert; aqwat al-dār likewise means a place became empty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r14.anchor: وأقوى دخل في الأرض القواء، ومنه أقوت الدار، وأقوى الطلل: أي صار قواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r15.claim: He rejects deriving this sense from the opposite phrase aqwā al-rajul, when his mount grew strong: that is a different verb, like atraba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r15.anchor: ومن قال: إن أقوى من الأضداد من حيث يقال: أقوى الرجل إذا قويت دابته فقد أخطأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r16.claim: Rich and poor alike need fire, especially against the cold, and nothing serves that need as well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p249/r16.anchor: والفقير والغني إذا أقوى سواء في الحاجة إلى النار، ولا شيء يغني غناءها في الصرد،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r1.claim: Seeing fire reminds people of Hell and its feared punishment, prompting them to seek refuge with God from it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون إذا رآها الرائي ذكر نار جهنم وما يخاف من عذابها فاستجار بالله منها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say al-muqwin means travelers; Ibn Qutayba relates the name to their lodging in barren country, where fire drives away beasts and guides the lost.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r2.anchor: أنهم المسافرون قاله ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك قال ابن قتيبة سموا بذلك لنزلهم القوى وهو القفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r3.claim: Mujahid says al-muqwin includes both travelers and settled people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r3.anchor: والثاني أنهم المسافرون والحاضرون قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the word means hungry people in Arabic.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r4.anchor: والثالث أنهم الجائعون قال ابن زيد المقوي الجائع في كلام العرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets them as people with no provisions and no place to return to.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p149#4/r5.anchor: والرابع أنهم الذين لا زاد معهم ولا مرد لهم قاله أبو عبيدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret the kindled fire as a reminder of the greater Fire, Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة: أي تذكر النار الكبرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r2.claim: Qatada transmits a mursal Prophetic report that earthly fire is one part out of seventy of Hellfire; when people say it suffices, the Prophet replies that it was struck with water twice so people can benefit from and approach it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يا قوم، ناركم هذه التي توقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said earthly fire is one of seventy parts of Hellfire and was struck by the sea twice; otherwise God would have made no one benefit from it. Ahmad transmits this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن ناركم هذه جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r4.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, the Prophet says human fire is one of seventy parts of Hellfire; when told it is sufficient, he says Hellfire exceeds it by sixty-nine parts. Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report; another Muslim wording says all sixty-nine are as hot as it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r4.anchor: نار بني آدم التي يوقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits from Abu Hurayra that Hellfire is seventy times darker than earthly fire; al-Diya al-Maqdisi notes Ibn Musʿab transmitted it from Malik without raising it to the Prophet and considers it to meet the conditions of sound hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p541#2/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أتدرون ما مثل ناركم هذه من نار جهنم؟ لهي أشد سوادا من

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Nadr ibn ʿArabi understand those who benefit as travelers; Ibn Jarir prefers this, deriving it from the expression that a house is left empty when its inhabitants depart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، والنضر بن عربي: معنى {للمقوين} المسافرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r2.claim: Another view derives the word from al-qiy and al-qiwa, meaning a barren, empty, distant place far from settled areas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: القي والقواء: القفر الخالي البعيد من العمران

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam interprets those who benefit as the hungry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r3.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: المقوي هنا الجائع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r4.claim: Mujahid, in reports from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym and Sufyan from Jabir al-Juʿfi, says the benefit is for residents and travelers and for any food that needs fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r4.anchor: وقال ليث ابن أبي سليم، عن مجاهد: {ومتاعا للمقوين} للحاضر والمسافر، لكل طعام لا يصلحه إلا النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r5.claim: In Ibn Abi Najih's report, Mujahid interprets those who benefit as all people who enjoy it; ʿIkrima is also reported to hold this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد قوله: {للمقوين} المستمتعين، الناس أجمعين. وكذا ذكر عن عكرمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r6.claim: The all-people interpretation is broader: rich and poor, residents and nomads need fire for cooking, warmth, light, and other uses. God put it in stones and pure iron, so travelers could carry tools and kindle it as needed; travelers are named though the benefit is universal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r6.anchor: وهذا التفسير أعم من غيره، فإن الحاضر والبادي من غني وفقير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r7.claim: A report through a man from the Muhajirun of Qarn says Muslims share three things: fire, pasture, and water; Ahmad and Abu Dawud transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r7.anchor: عن رجل من المهاجرين من قرن، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "المسلمون شركاء في ثلاثة: النار والكلأ والماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet said three things may not be withheld: water, pasture, and fire; Ibn Majah transmits it with a good chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ثلاث لا يمنعن: الماء والكلأ والنار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas adds that charging for these shared items is forbidden, but its chain contains the weak narrator ʿAbd Allah ibn Kharrash ibn Hawshab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p542/r9.anchor: وله من حديث ابن عباس مرفوعا مثل هذا وزيادة: "وثمنه حرام" (4) . ولكن في إسناده "عبد الله بن خراش بن حوشب" وهو ضعيف

BURSEVI:v9p273/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273/r8.claim: The tinder fire reminds people of Hell because they rely on earthly fire for livelihood and should remember the promised Fire; it is also a model of Hell.
BURSEVI:v9p273/r8.anchor: جعلنا نار الزناد تذكير النار جهنم من حيث عقلنا بها أسباب المعاش لينظروا إليها ويذكروا ما أوعدوا به

BURSEVI:v9p273/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p273/r9.claim: The Prophet says the fire people kindle is one seventieth of Hellfire’s heat.
BURSEVI:v9p273/r9.anchor: ناركم هذه التي يوقدها بنو آدم جزء من سبعين جزأ من حر جهنم

BURSEVI:v9p273/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273/r10.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p273/r10.claim: Another view takes the fire as proof of resurrection, since producing fire from a moist tree is an extraordinary transformation.
BURSEVI:v9p273/r10.anchor: وقيل تبصرة في أمر البعث فإنه ليس أبدع من إخراج النار من الشيء الرطب

BURSEVI:v9p273/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273/r11.speaker: عين المعاني
BURSEVI:v9p273/r11.claim: Ayn al-Maʿani treats the fire as evidence against deniers of punishment in the grave.
BURSEVI:v9p273/r11.anchor: وفي عين المعاني وهو حجة على منكري عذاب القبر

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r1.claim: Mataʿ means benefit and provision; producing fire is useful because making or carrying it is difficult.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r1.anchor: ومنفعه وبلغة لأن حمل النار يشق

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r2.claim: Al-Muqwīn are people staying in barren country without water, speech, or buildings, especially travelers.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r2.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء بالفتح وهو القفر الخالي عن الماء والكلام والعمارة وهم المسافرون

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r3.claim: Travelers especially need fire to drive away beasts, warm themselves, dry clothes, and cook; settled people nearby are less dependent on kindling.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r3.anchor: وتخصيصهم بذلك لأنهم أحوج إليها ليهرب منها السباع ويسطلوا من البرد ويجففوا ثيابهم ويصلحوا طعامهم

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r4.claim: Mentioning worldly usefulness after the reminder of Hell signals that the afterlife benefit is more important.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r4.anchor: وتأخير هذه المنفعة للتنبيه على أن الأهم هو النفع الأخروي

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r5.claim: The verb aqwā means to lodge in barren land, just as aṣḥara means to enter the desert.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r5.anchor: يقال أقوى الرجل إذا نزل في الأرض القواء كأصحر إذا دخل في الصحراء

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r6.claim: The Prophet asks Gabriel why he never sees Michael smile; Gabriel answers that Michael has not laughed since the Fire was created.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r6.anchor: قال النبي عليه السلام لجبريل مالي أر ميكائيل ضاحكا قط

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r7.speaker: أنس
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r7.claim: Anas transmits that the least punished person in Hell wears two sandals that make his brain boil, showing Hell exceeds worldly fire; the narrator asks God for protection.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r7.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه يرفعه أن أدنى أهل النار عذابا الذي يجعل له نعلان يغلي منهما دماغه

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r8.speaker: أبو الحسين المنصور
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r8.claim: The inward fire is love, kindled by the seeker’s striking in the sincere lover’s heart; its tree is eternal divine care, which Abu al-Husayn al-Mansur defines as the reality of love.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r8.anchor: وشجرتها هي العناية الإلهية السرمدية يدل هذا التأويل قول العارف أبي الحسين المنصور قدس سره

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r9.speaker: أبو الحسين المنصور
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r9.claim: Al-Mansur says without eternal divine care, a person would not know the Book or faith.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r9.anchor: حين سئل عن حقيقة المحبة هي العناية الإلهية السرمدية لولاها ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r10.claim: The fire guides human souls toward the path of truth, while its provision is spiritual food for lovers who abstain from food and drink for many days.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r10.anchor: نحن جعلناها تذكرة لأرباب النفوس البشرية ليهتدوا بنورها إلى سلوك طرق الحق ومتاعا للمقوين أي غذاء لأرواح المحبين

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r11.speaker: سهل التستري
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r11.claim: Sahl al-Tustari is said to have fasted for thirty days at a time.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r11.anchor: حكي عن سعل التستري رحمه الله أنه كان يطوي ثلاثين يوما

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r12.speaker: أبو عقيل المغربي
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r12.claim: Abu ʿAqil al-Maghribi is said to have eaten nothing for two years while residing in Mecca; the author also mentions many ascetic wayfarers.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r12.anchor: وعن أبي عقيل المغربي قدس سره أنه ما أكل سنتين وهو مجاور بمكة وعن كثير من المرتاضين السالكين

BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r13.claim: The commentary says Idris reached the fourth heaven through extreme detachment: he left bodily life, associated with angels, spent sixteen years without sleep, food, or marriage, and rose to the sphere of the Sun.
BURSEVI:v9p273#2/r13.anchor: وإنما رفع إدريس عليه السلام إلى السماء الرابعة لمبالغته في التجريد والترويح حتى أن الروحانية غلبت عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r3.claim: The fire is a reminder of Hell because ordinary livelihood depends on fire, keeping it constantly before people as a sign of the threatened punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r3.anchor: تذكيرا لنار جهنهم ، حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعايش كلها ، وعممنا بالحاجة إليها البلوى لتكون حاضرة للناس ينظرون إليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the fire is a reminder and model of Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r4.anchor: أو جعلناها تذكرة وأنموذجا من جهنم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says the fire people kindle is one seventieth of Hell's heat; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r5.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r7.claim: Al-muqwīn can mean people who lodge in barren country, or people whose bellies or provisions are empty; aqwaytu can mean going days without food.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p465#2/r7.anchor: للذين ينزلون القواء وهي القفر . أو للذين خلت بطونهم أو مزاودهم من الطعام . يقال : أقويت من أيام ، أي لم آكل شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r5.claim: Qatada says the fire is a reminder of the greater fire of the Hereafter.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r6.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r6.claim: Mujahid understands the fire as a means of seeing through darkness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r6.anchor: قاله مجاهد . { ومتاعا للمقوين } فيه خمسة أقاويل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r7.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the fire is a benefit for travelers; al-Farra explains that travelers are called al-muqwīn when they camp in barren land.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r7.anchor: منفعة للمسافرين قاله الضحاك ، قال الفراء : إنما يقال للمسافرين إذا نزلوا القي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r8.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r8.claim: Mujahid says the fire benefits anyone who enjoys it, whether settled or traveling.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fire serves hungry people when they prepare food.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r9.anchor: قاله ابن زيد . الرابع : الضعفاء والمساكين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r10.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r10.claim: Ibn Isa takes al-muqwīn as the weak and poor, deriving it from an empty, uninhabited home.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r10.anchor: حكاه ابن عيسى . والعرب تقول قد أقوى الرجل إذا ذهب ماله

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r11.claim: Arabic usage also calls a person aqwā when he has lost his wealth; al-Nabigha's verse depicts travelers left with only a fire drill and kindling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p461/r11.anchor: والعرب تقول قد أقوى الرجل إذا ذهب ماله , قال النابغة : يقوى بها الركب

MUJAHID:v2p651/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p651/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p651/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the reminder as the great fire, which reminds people of the fire of Hell.
MUJAHID:v2p651/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ نحن جعلناها تذكرة ﴾ يعني النار الكبرى يقول تذكرون بها نار جهنم

MUJAHID:v2p651/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p651/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p651/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the fire's usefulness as a benefit for all people who make use of it.
MUJAHID:v2p651/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ للمقوين ﴾ يعني للمستمتعين للناس أجمعين

MUQATIL:56:68-73/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r6.claim: The earthly fire reminds people of the greater fire of Hell.
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r6.anchor: { نحن جعلناها } هذه النار التي في الدنيا { تذكرة } لنار جهنم الكبرى

MUQATIL:56:68-73/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r7.claim: The fire is a provision for travelers in open country and for Bedouins.
MUQATIL:56:68-73/r7.anchor: يعنى متاعا للمسافرين لمن كان بأرض فلاة وللأعراب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r1.claim: Fire reminds people of Hell: God made livelihood depend on it so everyone needs it, sees it, and recalls the threatened punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r1.anchor: تذكير النار جهنم حيث علقنا بها أسباب المعاش عممنا بالحاجة اليها البلوى لتكون حاضرة للناس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r2.claim: Fire is a benefit for travelers lodging in desert country, or for people whose stomachs or provisions are empty; aqwat al-dār means a house became empty.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r2.anchor: للمسافرين النازلين في القواء وهي القفر أو الذين خلت بطونهم أو مزاودهم من الطعام من قولهم أقوت الدار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r3.claim: The passage moves from human creation to grain that sustains life, then water used with food, then fire for baking; food depends on these three, indispensable while the body lives.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p211#5/r3.anchor: بدأ بذكر خلق الانسان فقال أفرأيتم ما تمنون لأن النعمة فيه سابقة على جميع النعم ثم بما به قوامه وهو الحب

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r9.claim: Since God is the inventor and creator, people should thank Him and not deny His power to resurrect.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r9.anchor: أي المخترعون الخالقون أي فإذا عرفتم قدرتي فاشكروني

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r10.claim: Qatada says worldly fire is a reminder of the greater fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r10.anchor: يعني نار الدنيا موعظة للنار الكبرى قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r11.claim: Mujahid says fire is a light by which people see through darkness.

QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r12.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r12.claim: The Prophet says human fire is one part in seventy of Hellfire; when Companions said it sufficed, he explained that the other sixty-nine parts are each as hot as it.
QURTUBI-FULL:56:69-73/r12.anchor: وصح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r1.claim: The fire is a reminder of Hell: seeing an earthly fire should make a sensible person fear God and His punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r1.anchor: تذكرة لنار القيامة فيجب على العاقل أن يخشى الله تعالى وعذابه إذا رأى النار الموقدة

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r2.claim: It also reminds people that resurrection is possible: the One who places fire in green trees can place innate heat in a dead body.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r2.anchor: وثانيهما : تذكرة بصحة البعث ، لأن من قدر على إيداع النار

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r3.claim: Al-muqwī is the one who kindles the fire, strengthens it, and adds to it.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r3.anchor: والمقوي : هو الذي أوقده فقواه وزاده

RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r4.claim: The afterlife reminder comes before worldly use to show that the benefit of the next life is more complete and more worthy of attention.
RAZI-FULL:v29p160#4/r4.anchor: قدم كونها تذكرة على كونها متاعا ليعلم أن الفائدة الأخروية أتم وبالذكر أهم

STUDYQURAN:56:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r1.claim: Fire reminds people of the Resurrection or the Fire of Hell.
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r1.anchor: Fire is a reminder insofar as it reminds one of the Resurrection or the Fire in Hell

STUDYQURAN:56:71/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r2.claim: The Prophet says the fire people kindle has only one seventieth of Hell’s heat.
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r2.anchor: the Prophet said, “This fire of yours that human beings kindle contains but a seventieth of the heat in Hell”

STUDYQURAN:56:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r3.claim: Muqwīn, translated “desert dwellers,” can also mean all travelers.
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r3.anchor: Desert dwellers translates muqwīn, which can also refer to all travelers

STUDYQURAN:56:71/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r4.claim: Some understand those who enjoy the fire as everyone who benefits from using fire.
STUDYQURAN:56:71/r4.anchor: is taken by some as a reference to everyone who benefits from the use of fire

TAB-FULL:v22p356/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r1.claim: God made the fire a reminder of the greater Fire of Hell so that people may reflect and take admonition.
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {تذكرة} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «تذكرة النار الكبرى»

TAB-FULL:v22p356/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses “a reminder” as a reminder of the greater Fire.
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {تذكرة} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «تذكرة النار الكبرى»

TAB-FULL:v22p356/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r3.claim: Qatada says the earthly fire reminds people of the greater Fire; he transmits the Prophet's statement that this fire is one seventieth of Hell's fire and was cooled with water for human use.
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أفرأيتم النار التي تورون أأنتم أنشأتم شجرتها أم نحن المنشئون نحن جعلناها تذكرة}

TAB-FULL:v22p356/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r4.claim: The Prophet says the earthly fire is one part in seventy of Hell's fire; it was cooled twice so people could benefit from it and approach it.
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r4.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «ناركم هذه التي توقدون جزء من سبعين جزءا من نار جهنم»

TAB-FULL:v22p356/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r5.claim: Mujahid says the reminder points to the great fire of the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v22p356/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، {تذكرة} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «للنار الكبرى التي في الآخرة»

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the people who benefit from the fire as travelers.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «للمسافرين»

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r2.claim: Qatada explains المقوين as travelers, including those who are without provisions.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ومتاعا للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال " للمرمل: المسافر "

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak also says المقوين means travelers.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ومتاعا للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «للمسافرين»

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r4.claim: Mujahid says the fire is provision for those who enjoy it, meaning all people.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ومتاعا للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] «للمستمتعين، الناس أجمعين»

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r5.claim: In another report Mujahid includes both travelers and residents among those who enjoy the fire.

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r6.speaker: خصيف
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r6.claim: Khasif glosses the beneficiaries as all creatures.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r6.anchor: عن خصيف، في قوله: {ومتاعا للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «للخلق»

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says المقوي means a hungry person; in Arabic, “I have not eaten from it” means I ate none of it.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومتاعا للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال: " المقوي: الجائع في كلام العرب، يقول: أقويت منه كذا وكذا: ما أكلت منه

TAB-FULL:v22p357/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r8.claim: Al-Tabari prefers travelers without provisions, deriving the term from a dwelling becoming empty of inhabitants.
TAB-FULL:v22p357/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {للمقوين} [الواقعة: 73] قال: «للمسافرين»

TAB-FULL:v22p358/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r1.claim: Al-Tabari cites a poem in which أقوى means a place became empty of its inhabitants, supporting his derivation of المقوين.
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r1.anchor:
أقوى وأقفر من نعم وغيرها … هوج الرياح بهابي الترب موار
يعني بقوله: «أقوى» : خلا من سكانه،

TAB-FULL:v22p358/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r2.claim: Outside this context, المقوي can also mean someone with a strong horse or someone possessing much wealth.
TAB-FULL:v22p358/r2.anchor: وقد يكون المقوي: ذا الفرس القوي، وذا المال الكثير في غير هذا الموضع

SULAMI:v2p301#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p301#5/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p301#5/r1.claim: Ja'far says the fire is a warning for the pious and a means of conveyance for the gnostic saints.
SULAMI:v2p301#5/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : موعظة للمتقين وآله للأولياء من العارفين في حمله .

AKHFASH:v2p533/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p533/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p533/r1.claim: المقوين means travelers in barren land; أقوى الشيء describes something from which everything has gone.
AKHFASH:v2p533/r1.anchor: وقال {متاعا للمقوين} اي للمسافرين في الأرض القي. تقول: "أقوى الشيء" إذا ذهب كل ما فيه

THALABI:v9p216/r26.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p216/r26.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p216/r26.claim: God made the fire of this world as a reminder of the greater fire of the afterlife.
THALABI:v9p216/r26.anchor: نحن جعلناها يعني نار الدنيا تذكرة للنار الكبرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r5.claim: The fire is an admonition from which a believer should take heed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r5.anchor: قال عطاء: موعظة ليتعظ بها المؤمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r6.claim: The fire is a worldly reminder of the fire of Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عظة في الدنيا من نار جهنم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r7.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r7.claim: This fire reminds people of the greater fire, Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة، ومجاهد ومقاتل: جعلنا هذه النار تذكرة للنار الكبرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r8.claim: Seeing fire reminds its observer of Hell and feared punishment, prompting remembrance of God and seeking refuge from it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r8.anchor: أي إذا رآها الرائي ذكر جهنم وما يخافه من العذاب فذكر الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r9.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r9.claim: A muqwin is someone who alights in barren land; the word includes any traveler passing through or resident there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r9.anchor: قال الفراء، والزجاج: المقوي الذي ينزل بالقواء وهي الأرض الخالية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r10.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r10.claim: Aqwa describes a group that has arrived in a barren tract of land.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r10.anchor: قال الليث: أقوى القوم إذا وقعوا في قي من الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r11.claim: The beneficiaries are people of the wilderness and travelers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ينتفع بها أهل البوادي والأسفار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r12.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r12.claim: The fire benefits travelers who alight in barren country.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r12.anchor: وقال الكلبي: منفعة للمسافرين النازلين في الأرض القي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r13.speaker: مقاتل والحسن والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r13.claim: They take it as a benefit for those in barren country, including Bedouins; travelers are singled out because they need fire more than settled people, including to drive away beasts at night and meet many needs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول: ومنافع لمن كان بأرض في ومنهم الأعراب (¬8)، ونحو هذا قال الحسن والضحاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r14.claim: The traveler has greater need of fire: Bedouins must light it at night to keep wild animals away and for many other needs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r14.anchor: لأن منفعته بها أكثر من منفعة المقيم، وذلك أن أهل البوادي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r15.claim: A muqwin is one with no provisions or wealth; the word draws on aqwat al-dar, a house becoming empty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r15.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: المقوي الذي لا زاد معه ولا مال، وهذا من قولهم أقوت الدار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r16.speaker: الربيع والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r16.claim: The term means needy people without provisions, who need to light a fire to roast hunted meat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r16.anchor: وهذا قول الربيع، والسدي. قالا: يعني المرملين المقترين الذين لا زاد معهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r17.claim: Al-ʿAwfī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās the interpretation that the beneficiaries are those left without provisions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r17.anchor: وهذه رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r18.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r18.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r18.claim: The word covers everyone who enjoys fire, resident or traveler: people use it for light, warmth, cooking, and baking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p253/r18.anchor: وفي المقوين قول ثالث، وهو قول عكرمة، ومجاهد، قالا: للمقوين أي للمستمتعين بها من الناس أجمعين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r1.claim: The fire is a reminder that makes people remember Hell.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r3.claim: Al-muqwīn are travelers, named for lodging in al-qawāʾ, the empty desert.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r3.anchor: سموا بذلك: لنزولهم القواء وهو: القفر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says al-muqwī is someone with no provisions, from aqwā al-rajul when his provisions run out.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: "المقوي: الذي لا زاد معه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers the traveler gloss and rejects Abu Ubayda's gloss: a person without provisions is not more in need of the fire than one with provisions; he says the latter is more in need.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p451#5/r5.anchor: ولا أرى التفسير إلا الأول؛ ولا أرى الذي لا زاد معه أولى بالنار ولا أحوج إليها من الذي معه الزاد.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r6.claim: A second sense is benefit; Ibn Qutayba explains the uninhabited houses as inns that shelter visitors from heat and cold.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p558/r6.anchor: والثاني : المنفعة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة
